points.description: States that a queue is a data structure that stores elements and removes them in first-in-first-out order (the first item added is the first removed; equivalently, items are removed in the order they were added).
points.partial_credit: Award about 2-3 marks for a vague or incomplete answer, e.g. says it is a data structure/collection/line for storing elements but gives no or unclear ordering, or gives only the ordering without saying it stores elements.

rubric.notes: Full marks for stating that a queue stores elements and works first-in-first-out (FIFO), in any wording, including informal ones like "like a line, first one in comes out first". Part marks for a related but incomplete answer, such as only "a data structure to store items" or mention of enqueue/dequeue without the ordering. Give no marks if the answer describes last-in-first-out (a stack) or is unrelated. Ignore the model answer's slip "last item added will be last removed", which is consistent with FIFO. Extra correct detail is fine.
